properties.name: reflow2 declares every relation it derives as data, a check holds the declarations to the code, and a served read evaluates them over a design
properties.source: Anthony, 2026-09-29, in the dev_reflow2 hub session, relayed by the hub agent: "Fix all the root causes and go with the 7 ideas you'd promote". This is idea 6, dec:idea-a-served-read-evaluates-every-derived-relation-reflow2-computes.
properties.statement:
Every relation reflow2 derives is DECLARED as data: its rule, the primitive it reads as, whether it is deduced or induced, and the code that computes it. This covers the 23 identified by the graph-primitives study, today hand-written across about 15 source files, including the blast-radius closure. A check fails when the code derives a relation nothing declares, or a declaration names code that does not compute it. A served read evaluates the declared relations over a design and reports each one's count, and the derived-to-asserted ratio, without a hand-written script.

This is the "every relationship it derives is a declared rule" half of req:reflow2s-code-reasons-from-the-declared-meanings-and-every-derived-relationship-is-a-declared-rule (test 3). That broader requirement stays proposed. This part is accepted.

Counter-argument kept: declarations kept beside hand-written code are a second copy, honest only while a test checks them against the code. So the check is part of the requirement, not a follow-up.

Found by the two-agent exercise (I20): the derived-to-asserted ratio took a ~150-line script over the export.
